fields.h1: Build a Wedding Landing Page That Keeps Every Guest Informed
fields.hero_description: Create a wedding landing page from one prompt, with your date and travel details up top and guest replies in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Wedding Page
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the page your guests open and the database that keeps every answer they send.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from your plans

Describe the day to Emergent: where and when it happens, and what each guest needs to tell you before it. It builds the page and its forms, and another prompt changes either one.
fields.feature_2:
Guest answers in a database you own

The app keeps each person's answers in a database you own, from the reply and the meal to the hotel and the shuttle seat. Seating plans start from one table, not a dozen texts.
fields.feature_3:
Emails that go out without you

Tell the app who should hear about what, and it sends email, Slack, or in-app alerts and reminders. Anyone who has not answered gets a nudge; your coordinator gets the list.
fields.feature_4:
Linked to the tools you plan with

Built apps connect to any tool with an API. Replies can sync out to the spreadsheet or planning tool you already keep; pick the one your coordinator uses, and you share one list.
fields.feature_5:
Your names as the address

Put the page on a custom domain made of your two names; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. A short address fits on the save-the-date card you mail.
fields.feature_6:
Free to start, exportable later

The free tier covers building and publishing your wedding page. Paid plans include full code export to your GitHub repository, and a friend who codes can reuse the site later.

fields.tab_content_1:
Hotel links went to 7 guests who had not answered

Hana Yoon and Felix Quarles booked a block of rooms near their venue, and their page asks each of the 70 guests coming where they are staying. By April 5, 52 had picked the block hotel and 11 had picked somewhere else. That morning the app emailed the hotel link and the booking cutoff to the 7 who had not answered.
fields.tab_content_2:
The coordinator sees all 54 shuttle riders by departure

Guests at Josie Tremblay and Malik Stroud's vineyard wedding pick a seat on the 4:00 pm or the 4:30 pm shuttle when they reply. The app keeps each choice with the rider's name and emails one list to their coordinator, Bette Lachance: 38 riders on the first shuttle and 16 on the second.
fields.tab_content_3:
The DJ got all 63 song requests in one email

The reply form on Imogen Ingram and Theo Dorsey's page ends with one optional question: which song gets you dancing? A week before the wedding, the app emailed their DJ, Sol Bellamy-Cho, all 63 requests in one list, each with the name of the guest who asked for it.
fields.tab_content_4:
A 3:30 start reached all 112 yes replies

Rain in the forecast pushed Ada Nkemelu and Sam Corriveau to move their ceremony from 4:00 pm to 3:30 pm. One prompt changed the time on their page, and the app emailed the new time to all 112 guests who had replied yes.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Wedding Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a wedding landing page from one clear ask to a tested page that keeps every guest answer in one table.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what every guest must do
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the essentials on the first screen
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Answer the travel questions up front
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the one answer you need from every guest, such as a reply by a set date, and build the page around it. Everything else on the page, from the schedule to the registry link, supports that answer.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A guest who opens the link from a text message should see your names, the date, the town, and the reply button without scrolling. Everything else can sit lower on the page.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Name the sections, every question on the reply form, and who should hear about each answer. From that one prompt, Emergent builds the whole page with its forms and their tables.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the nearest airport, the hotel block with its booking cutoff, parking, and any shuttle times. Each line you add here is one less text message asking for it.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask only what the day needs
fields.howto_step_5_des: Each question on the reply form should change something you plan, such as the meal count or the seating. Leave out anything you will not act on, and the form stays short on a phone.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Reply from your own phone as a guest would. Check that the row lands in the guest table and that every email you set up reaches the right person before the link goes on the save-the-date.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Keep the page current until the day
fields.howto_step_7_des: When a time or a place changes, update the page with one more prompt that same day. Then open it on a phone and make sure the old detail appears nowhere on it.

faq_plan.q: What is a wedding landing page?
faq_plan.a: A wedding landing page is the one page your guests open for everything about the day. It tells them when and where to be, and it gives them a way to reply. Think of it as the short version of a wedding website, with each guest question answered on a single scroll.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a wedding landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI landing page builder in plain words: your names and date, the sections you want, the questions guests should answer, and who hears about each reply. From that prompt, Emergent builds the forms, the tables behind them, and the page itself, and you change any of it later by prompting again. Write the reply form first, since every guest uses it.

faq_plan.q: What should a wedding website landing page include?
faq_plan.a: Put your names, the date and town, and a reply button at the top. Below that, add the schedule and the travel details, then a link to your registry, and keep the story of how you met for the end. If a section answers a question guests would otherwise text you, it belongs on the page.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a wedding landing page easy to use on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Build it the way you would build any mobile landing page: one column with large buttons, and a reply form with only the fields the day needs. Then open the page on your own phone the way a guest would, and fix anything you have to pinch or zoom to read.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect guest replies on a wedding landing page?
faq_plan.a: Add a reply form that asks for each guest's name, whether they are coming, and only the details you plan around, such as a meal choice. Built on Emergent, the app saves each reply as a row in a database you own, and the head count comes from that one table. Print a reply-by date right next to the button.

faq_plan.q: What should I do with my wedding landing page after the wedding?
faq_plan.a: Turn it into a thank-you note to your guests: replace the reply form with a few lines of thanks and a link to the photos. Keep the guest table, because the names in it are the start of your thank-you card list.

faq_plan.q: Is a wedding landing page for couples different from one for a wedding business?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A couple's page speaks to invited guests and collects their answers, while a planner or a venue needs a page that turns strangers into inquiries. If you send ad traffic to a wedding business page, build it as a ppc landing page. Lead with your packages and past weddings, and give it an inquiry form that asks for the date and the guest count.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep uninvited plus-ones off my wedding landing page?
faq_plan.a: Tie each invitation to a seat count. Print a short code on every invitation, and have the reply form offer only as many name fields as that code allows. An app built on Emergent can keep each code and its seat count in the guest table, which also gives you the number of seats promised.

faq_plan.q: When should a wedding landing page go live?
faq_plan.a: Publish it before the save-the-dates go out, because the card is where guests first see the link. Start with the venue and the hotel block, then add the reply form when the invitations are ready to mail.

faq_plan.q: Should a wedding landing page be one page or a full website?
faq_plan.a: One page is enough for a single ceremony and reception: a one page website with clear sections holds the details and the reply form. Move to several pages when you host a full weekend of separate events, each with its own timing and dress code. Either way, keep the reply button easy to reach from every section.
